about.title: Calistoga Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Calistoga is a small city, but its residents and visitors rely on the same consumer products, farm equipment, and vehicles used across Napa County — and defects in any of these can cause serious harm. California law generally allows injured people to pursue strict liability claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers, meaning you often don't have to prove anyone was careless, just that the product was defective and that defect caused your injury. This can apply to a car part that failed near Foothill Boulevard, a piece of vineyard or agricultural equipment, a household appliance, or a child's toy. Because Calistoga's economy leans on tourism, hospitality, and wine production, defective products in these settings — from spa equipment to farm machinery — can also lead to claims. If you were injured by a product anywhere in Calistoga, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can review what happened and explain your options.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Claim
items.desc: California often applies strict liability to defective products, so you may not need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the product was defective and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may give you more than one path toward accountability.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: An attorney can advise you to keep the product itself, since preserving it intact is often critical to proving a design, manufacturing, or warning defect.

items.question: What counts as a product defect under California law?
items.answer: California recognizes three main types: design defects, manufacturing defects, and failure-to-warn defects. A design defect means the product is unreasonably dangerous even when made correctly, while a manufacturing defect means something went wrong during production. A warning defect involves a failure to properly disclose known risks of using the product.

items.question: I was hurt by farm or vineyard equipment near Calistoga — does that count?
items.answer: Yes, product liability claims can apply to agricultural or vineyard equipment used in and around Calistoga, not just consumer goods. If a piece of machinery malfunctioned and caused injury, an independent attorney can evaluate whether a design or manufacturing defect played a role.

items.question: Do I need to keep the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Yes, whenever possible. Preserving the product in its post-incident condition can be important evidence for showing a defect existed, so avoid repairing, discarding, or altering it before speaking with an attorney.

items.question: Is there really no cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Correct, LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
